Issues.Title: fix(router): navigate every time a RedirectCommand is thrown from an error boundary
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`triggerRedirectIfCommand` marks the thrown `RedirectCommand` with a symbol so the redirect is only dispatched once. The mark is never cleared, so if the same `RedirectCommand` instance is thrown again (for example a shared constant), the router no longer navigates and the user stays on the failing route.

Issue Number: #72027

## What is the new behavior?

The mark is removed, so every thrown `RedirectCommand` navigates. As discussed in the issue, the mark is not needed: a redirect is handled by the first outlet that catches it and is not propagated further, so it is not seen by several outlets.

The design doc and the angular.dev guide no longer describe the deduplication.

A test covers throwing the same `RedirectCommand` instance twice. The existing test for nested outlets (`dispatches RedirectCommand only once when bubbling through multiple boundaries`) is unchanged.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Testing note: I could not run Bazel on my machine (Windows). I verified the behavior against the published `22.3.0-rc.0` router with the mark removed, using the repro from the issue and the nested-outlet scenario (with and without `defaultErrorComponent`): the repro now navigates both times and the nested case still dispatches exactly once. The added spec itself has not been run locally, so please rely on CI.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(router): navigate every time a RedirectCommand is thrown from an error boundary" (#72051)

Issues.Title: refactor(router): set route references on RouterState during activation
Issues.Body:
Split out from #72020 (first commit).

Remove `setRouterState` from the `RouterState` constructor and call it explicitly in `createEmptyState` and at the start of `ActivateRoutes.activate` instead of during `createRouterState`. Thread `parentRoute` through `setupAndRunResources` and `finalizeResources` so resource setup does not rely on `route.parent` before activation.

Because `createRouterState` runs before async work that can still cancel or redirect (and will move even earlier ahead of resolvers), setting `_routerState` there mutates reused `ActivatedRoute` instances prematurely and leaves their `firstChild` and `children` pointing at an uncommitted or abandoned tree if rollback occurs. Waiting until `ActivateRoutes.activate` keeps them on the current tree until activation, matching pre-1f287b9ba7 timing.

Related to b/584585009.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(router): set route references on RouterState during activation" (#72049)

Issues.Title: docs: describe the automatic Eager migration in the v22 update guide
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The v22 step `22.0.0-component-onpush-default` in the update guide tells readers to set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager` themselves to keep the previous behavior. It does not mention that `ng update @angular/core` runs the `change-detection-eager` migration, which adds that property to every component without a `changeDetection` property and replaces the deprecated `ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default` with `Eager`. Readers who follow the step add settings the migration already added, and readers who update without `ng update` get no hint that nothing was migrated for them.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

The step says what `ng update` changes, that `OnPush` components are left alone, what to do when updating without `ng update`, and that the explicit `Eager` can be removed once a component works with `OnPush`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

The migration's behavior is taken from `packages/core/schematics/migrations/change-detection-eager/migration.ts` and its spec.

Issues.Title: fix(common): normalize the exponent when rounding carries in exponential notation
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Numbers with more than 22 integer digits are formatted in exponential notation with a single integer digit in the mantissa. When rounding to the requested number of fraction digits carries into a new digit, `roundNumber` adds the carry to the mantissa instead of the exponent, so the result is not normalized:

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `formatNumber(9.99999e22, 'en')` | `10E+22` | `1E+23` |
| `formatNumber(9.99999e22, 'en', '1.2-2')` | `10.00E+22` | `1.00E+23` |
| `formatPercent(9.99999e22, 'en')` | `10E+24%` | `1E+25%` |
| `formatCurrency(9.99999e22, 'en', '$')` | `$10.00E+22` | `$1.00E+23` |

The same applies to `DecimalPipe`, `PercentPipe` and `CurrencyPipe`.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

In exponential notation the carry is folded into the exponent. All digits after the carry are zeros at that point, so the last one is dropped to keep the number of fraction digits unchanged. Numbers that are not in exponential notation are not affected.

The new spec fails without the change for every case that carries; the `'1.0-10'` case without a carry is included as a control.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(common): normalize the exponent when rounding carries in exponential notation" (#72044)

Issues.Title: fix(forms): skip deferred registration when the parent group is gone
Issues.Body:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`NgForm.addControl`/`addFormGroup` register in a microtask and call `container.registerControl` without a null check. When the parent group was removed before that microtask runs, `_findContainer` returns `null` and the registration throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'registerControl')` as an unhandled rejection, while the matching remove path is already null-safe.

Issue Number: #69440

## What is the new behavior?

The add paths skip the registration when the parent is gone, and `_findContainer` is typed `FormGroup | null` as suggested in the issue.

Tests: two new cases in `packages/forms/test/directives_spec.ts` (remove the parent group, then add a control / a nested group); both failed before the fix with the error above.

## What is the current behavior?

A `<select [formField]>` observes character data because an `<option>` without a `value` uses its text as value, but `isRelevantSelectMutation` only accepts records that add or remove nodes, which a `characterData` record never does. When an option's text changes to match the model value, the select stays on no selection.

Character data changes outside comments count as relevant, so the select resyncs.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): report field tree properties to the `in` operator
Issues.Body:

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

The `FieldTree` proxy has no `has` trap, so the `in` operator checks the proxy target (a function): `Symbol.iterator in field` is `false` for iterable object and array fields, `'x' in field` is `false` for an existing child, and `'name' in field` / `'length' in field` are `true` for every object field.

Issue Number: #70252

## What is the new behavior?

A `has` trap reports the same properties as `get`: child fields, `length` and `Symbol.iterator` for arrays, `Symbol.iterator` for objects. This matches the approach of the earlier draft #70253.

Tests: three new cases in `packages/forms/signals/test/node/field_proxy.spec.ts`; two failed before the fix.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): do not scope `&` selectors nested in `:host`
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Since nested CSS rules are scoped (22.2.0), a compound selector that starts with `&` inside a `:host` rule, such as `:host { &.md { ... } }`, gets the content attribute: `[_nghost-c1] { &.md[_ngcontent-c1] { ... } }`. There `&` is the host element, which does not carry that attribute, so the rule never matches. It shows wherever the compiler scopes nested CSS itself (for example JIT, or `encapsulateStyle(':host { &.md { width: 70px } }', 'c1')`); the CLI flattens nesting before AOT scoping.

Issue Number: #71050

## What is the new behavior?

`&` compound selectors (`&.md`, `&:hover`, `&[attr]`) nested in rules whose selectors all match the host element (`:host`, `:host(...)`, `:host-context(...)`) are left unscoped, also in deeper `&` rules. Descendant selectors (`& .child`, `.child`) are still scoped, and so are `&` selectors nested in e.g. `:host .item`.

Tests: four new cases in `packages/compiler/test/shadow_css/nesting_spec.ts`; three failed before the fix (the fourth pins the unchanged `:host .item` behaviour).

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

No public API change. The `@angular/compiler` package has no public API golden.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Issues.Title: ci: emit failure annotations using problem matchers and Bazel BEP
Issues.Body:
Alternative to #71938. Instead of wrapping `run:` commands, this uses GitHub Actions problem matchers plus a post step that reads the Bazel build event file, so the reason for a CI failure can be read from the check-run annotations API without downloading the job log.

- `.github/matchers/ci.json` has problem matchers for `tsc`, `tslint`, Bazel `ERROR:` lines, `ts-circular-deps` chains and `ng-dev` error lines.
- `scripts/ci/annotate-bazel-failures.mts` reads the build event file of the last Bazel invocation and prints one `::error` per failed target. Failed tests get the end of their test log, and build failures get the Bazel error followed by the compiler output. Flaky tests that passed on retry are skipped, nothing is printed if the last Bazel invocation succeeded, and anything past the 10 annotations GitHub keeps per step is summarized in the last one.
- `.github/actions/bazel-annotations` is a small local action that adds `--build_event_json_file` to `.bazelrc.user`, registers the matchers, and runs the script in a `post-if: failure()` step.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` registers the matchers and runs the script's unit tests in `lint`, and adds the action to the Bazel jobs. `pr.yml` is not changed.

Checked on a throwaway PR (#72047) that wires the same steps into `pr.yml` with intentional failures: a tslint error, a circular dependency, an invalid ngbot config, a `tsc` error, a failing Bazel test and a Bazel build failure.

Once the matching `angular/dev-infra` change (angular/dev-infra#4112) lands and is rolled in here, the local action, matcher file and script can be removed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "ci: emit failure annotations using problem matchers and Bazel BEP" (#72043)

Issues.Title: fix(service-worker): ignore all `only-if-cached` requests
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Chrome now sends the DevTools request for the page source with `mode: 'same-origin'`, so it slips past the `only-if-cached` guard in `Driver.onFetch()`. It then falls back on the network, misses the HTTP cache (e.g. `index.html` served with `no-store`) and `safeFetch()` answers it with a synthetic 504 that shows up in the page console.

Issue Number: #72032

## What is the new behavior?

The service worker skips every `only-if-cached` request, whatever its mode, and lets the browser answer it from its own HTTP cache.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Requests like this no longer get answered from the SW cache either, even for assets the SW has cached. I think that's fine since `only-if-cached` asks for the HTTP cache, and in practice it's mostly DevTools sending it, but I can narrow it to the network fallback if you'd prefer. The guard isn't a DevTools workaround anymore, so I dropped the TODO.

Issues.Title: fix(core): update attribute bindings inside ICU cases
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type - [x] Bugfix ## What is the current behavior? Attribute interpolations on elements inside an ICU case are not applied correctly: ```html
{count, plural, =0 {none} other {x}}
``` - If the attribute binding is the only binding in the case, the attribute is never set. - If the case also contains a text binding (e.g. `{{count}}`), the attribute is set once, but later changes to `title` are never reflected in the DOM. `walkIcuTree` discards the binding mask returned by `generateBindingUpdateOpCodes` for attribute interpolations, while it combines the mask for text bindings. `icuStart` only emits the `icuUpdateCase` opcode for (and only triggers it on) the bindings in that mask, so attribute bindings are left out. Issue Number: N/A ## What is the new behavior? The mask of attribute bindings is included in the ICU binding mask, so attribute bindings inside ICU cases are set when the case is created and updated when their value changes. New acceptance tests cover an attribute as the only binding in a case, an attribute next to a text binding, and an attribute on a nested element; all three fail without the change. The existing opcode expectation in `render3/i18n/i18n_spec.ts` (`other {�0� emails}`) encoded the old behavior (`mask & 0b1`) and now expects `mask & 0b11`. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(core): use the custom Sanitizer for URLs in i18n attributes
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type - [x] Bugfix ## What is the current behavior? Translated attributes with interpolations in a URL context, e.g. ```html
{count, plural, other {link}}
``` are sanitized at runtime by `i18nResolveSanitizer` with the raw `_sanitizeUrl` function. Unlike the `ɵɵsanitize*` instructions, it does not consult a `Sanitizer` provided by the application (`{provide: Sanitizer, useValue: ...}`). All other security contexts (HTML, style, script, resource URL) in the same function already use the `ɵɵsanitize*` instructions, and the compile-time path for static i18n attributes emits `ɵɵsanitizeUrl` as well, so URLs were the only inconsistent case. Issue Number: N/A ## What is the new behavior? `i18nResolveSanitizer` returns `ɵɵsanitizeUrl` for the URL context, so a custom `Sanitizer` is used for translated URL attributes just like for regular bindings. Without a custom `Sanitizer` the behavior is unchanged (`ɵɵsanitizeUrl` falls back to `_sanitizeUrl`). The new tests in `i18n_spec.ts` fail without the change (`Expected 'unsafe:javascript:…' to be 'custom:javascript:…'`) and pass with it. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [x] No

Issues.Title: service-worker: DevTools' only-if-cached request for the document now has mode 'same-origin' and is answered with a synthetic 504
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

service-worker

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When DevTools is opened on a page that was loaded while DevTools was closed, Chrome asks for the document's source with a request that goes through the service worker. The Angular service worker turns it into a synthetic `504 Gateway Timeout`, which shows up in the console of the page:

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 504 (Gateway Timeout)   http://localhost:8080/#/home
```

and DevTools itself reports `Content unavailable. Resource was not cached` for the document.

`Driver.onFetch()` already has a guard for exactly this DevTools request ([driver.ts#L270-L289](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/551c446d98e2512e793f7254d7eb4c932c2450ef/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L270-L289), from #22362):

```ts
// When opening DevTools in Chrome, a request is made for the current URL (and possibly related
// resources, e.g. scripts) with `cache: 'only-if-cached'` and `mode: 'no-cors'`. ...
if (req.cache === 'only-if-cached' && req.mode !== 'same-origin') {
```

but current Chrome (157) sends that request with `mode: 'same-origin'`, so the guard no longer matches. What a plain service worker sees for it:

```json
{"url":"http://localhost:8080/","mode":"same-origin","cache":"only-if-cached","destination":"","accept":"*/*","credentials":"include","redirect":"follow"}
```

From there:

1. `AppVersion.handleFetch()` returns `null`: it is not a navigation request (`mode` is not `navigate`, `Accept` is `*/*`) and the URL is not an asset.
2. `Driver.handleFetch()` falls back to `safeFetch(event.request)` ([driver.ts#L630-L632](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/551c446d98e2512e793f7254d7eb4c932c2450ef/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L630-L632)).
3. The request keeps `cache: 'only-if-cached'`. When the document is not in the HTTP cache, which is always the case when `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store` (a common setup so that the document is never stale), the fetch fails with `net::ERR_CACHE_MISS`.
4. `safeFetch()` catches it and answers `504 Gateway Timeout` with an empty body ([driver.ts#L1375-L1385](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/551c446d98e2512e793f7254d7eb4c932c2450ef/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L1375-L1385)).

`/ngsw/state` then logs, for every such request:

```
TypeError(Failed to fetch, TypeError: Failed to fetch
    at Driver.safeFetch (http://localhost:8080/ngsw-worker.js:2257:33)
    at Driver.handleFetch (http://localhost:8080/ngsw-worker.js:1857:23)) Driver.fetch(http://localhost:8080/#/home)
```

Nothing breaks for the user (the page itself is served normally), but every app using the service worker with a non-cacheable `index.html` gets a "504" in the console whenever someone opens DevTools. That looks like a server problem and sends people investigating their gateway.

**Suggested fix:** do not handle `only-if-cached` requests at all, whatever their mode, so that the browser answers them from its own HTTP cache as it would without a service worker:

```ts
if (req.cache === 'only-if-cached') {
  return;
}
```

An `only-if-cached` request explicitly asks not to touch the network, so `safeFetch()` can never do anything useful with it. Alternatively, `safeFetch()` could return `Response.error()` instead of a synthetic 504 for such requests.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No hosted reproduction: it needs a service worker and a specific `Cache-Control` header. Steps:

1. `ng new repro --routing --ssr=false && cd repro && ng add @angular/pwa`, optionally with `withHashLocation()`.
2. `ng build`, then serve `dist/repro/browser` with `Cache-Control: no-store` on `index.html`. With `npx http-server -c-1`, `index.html` stays in the HTTP cache and the request succeeds, so the header matters.
3. Open the app in Chrome, wait for the service worker to take control, and reload with DevTools **closed**.
4. Open DevTools: the console shows `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 504 (Gateway Timeout)` for the page URL, and `/ngsw/state` shows the `Driver.fetch(...)` entry above.

With DevTools already open during the load, nothing happens: DevTools then has the document from the load and does not ask for it again.

The request can also be triggered without the DevTools UI, through CDP: attach to the page after it loaded and call `Page.getResourceContent` for the main frame's URL. It returns `Content unavailable. Resource was not cached`, and the 504 appears in the page's log.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 504 (Gateway Timeout)
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Angular           : 22.2.4
Node.js           : 24.19.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.17.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

@angular/service-worker 22.2.4 (the code above is unchanged on main)
Browser: Google Chrome 157.0.8103.51 (macOS)
```

### Anything else?

The guard comment says "This is likely a bug in Chrome DevTools" and has a TODO to remove it once DevTools is fixed. Chrome now sends the request with `mode: 'same-origin'`, which makes the `only-if-cached` request valid, so it falls through to the regular handling instead.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "service-worker: DevTools' only-if-cached request for the document now has mode 'same-origin' and is answered with a synthetic 504" (#72032)

Issues.Title: Router error boundaries: a reused RedirectCommand instance only redirects the first time
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No (new in 22.3.0-rc.0: route error boundaries)

### Description

With `withErrorBoundaries()`, throwing a `RedirectCommand` from a routed component is supposed to always navigate (see `packages/router/docs/error_boundaries.md`, "The Rule: `RedirectCommand` Always Navigates").

To avoid dispatching the same redirect several times while it bubbles through nested outlets, `triggerRedirectIfCommand` in `router_error_boundary.ts` tags the `RedirectCommand` object itself with a `REDIRECT_DISPATCHED` symbol and skips the navigation if the tag is already set. The tag is never cleared, so if the same `RedirectCommand` **instance** is thrown again later (a module-level constant, a field on a service, a cached value), the router no longer navigates. The user stays on the failing route with the error component rendered.

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
const toLogin = new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/login')); // created once and reused

@Component({template: 'A'})
class Guarded {
  constructor() {
    throw toLogin;
  }
}

provideRouter(
  [
    {path: '', component: Home},
    {path: 'a', component: Guarded},
    {path: 'login', component: Login},
  ],
  withErrorBoundaries({defaultErrorComponent: ErrorCmp}),
);

await router.navigateByUrl('/a'); // -> /login (correct)
await router.navigateByUrl('/');
await router.navigateByUrl('/a'); // expected /login, but the router stays on /a and renders ErrorCmp
```

Confirmed on `@angular/router@22.3.0-rc.0`. The relevant code on `main` has not changed since the feature landed.

### Expected

Every time a `RedirectCommand` is thrown from a routed component the router navigates, regardless of whether the instance was thrown before. De-duplication should only apply to the same occurrence bubbling through several outlets.

### Notes / possible directions

- Workaround: always throw a new `RedirectCommand`.
- The de-duplication could be scoped to one bubbling pass instead of the lifetime of the instance, for example by clearing the mark in a microtask after it is set, or by tracking dispatched commands in a `WeakSet` that is reset when the navigation that rendered the failing outlet ends.
- Writing a symbol property onto a user-supplied object also throws in strict mode if that object is frozen; a `WeakSet` would avoid that as well.

Happy to send a PR if the direction is agreed.

### Angular version

22.3.0-rc.0 and `main`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Router error boundaries: a reused RedirectCommand instance only redirects the first time" (#72027)

Issues.Title: fix(common): include binary request bodies in the HTTP transfer cache key
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) — not needed, no public API change

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`makeCacheKey` in the HTTP transfer cache only adds string and `URLSearchParams` bodies to the cache key. For every other body type (`ArrayBuffer`, `Blob`, `FormData`) it uses an empty string.

Since `HttpClient.query()` made `QUERY` requests cacheable by default, two `QUERY` requests to the same URL with different `ArrayBuffer` bodies share a cache key. On the server the second request is answered from the cache of the first one without hitting the network, and the wrong response ends up in `TransferState`. The same happens for `POST` requests that opt in with `transferCache: true`.

Reproduction (server mode, `HttpTestingController`): `http.query('/api/search', bodyA)` followed by `http.query('/api/search', bodyB)` returns the response of `bodyA` for both, with a single `TransferState` entry.

Fixes #72026

## What is the new behavior?

- `ArrayBuffer` bodies are included in the cache key (base64 of the bytes).
- `FormData` bodies with only string entries are included in the cache key (ordered entries).
- Bodies whose contents can only be read asynchronously (`Blob`, `FormData` containing files) cannot be keyed, so those requests are no longer cached, instead of colliding on one key.
- String, JSON and `URLSearchParams` bodies behave as before.

The prefixes used for the binary kinds contain `\0` so that a string body cannot produce the same key as a binary body with equivalent content.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Requests with a `Blob` body or a `FormData` body containing files, which were previously cached under a shared key, are no longer cached. Their cached responses were not reliable, since different bodies received the same response.

## Other information

Testing note: I could not run Bazel on my machine (Windows). I ran the updated `transfer_cache_spec.ts` through a local vitest/jsdom harness against the changed sources: the 7 added tests pass (5 of them fail without the change), and the remaining failures are the same 12 that fail before the change because they rely on Jasmine-only APIs in that harness. Please let CI be the source of truth.

Open question for reviewers: for very large `ArrayBuffer` bodies the whole content is base64-encoded and hashed. If that is a concern, a size cap (skip caching above it) or hashing the bytes directly would be easy follow-ups.

Issues.Title: HTTP transfer cache: QUERY/POST requests with different binary bodies share one cache key
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No (the cache-key gap pre-dates it, but `HttpClient.query()` made `QUERY` requests cacheable by default, which exposes it)

### Description

The HTTP transfer cache builds its key in `makeCacheKey` (`packages/common/http/src/transfer_cache.ts`). Only string and `URLSearchParams` bodies are added to the key; every other body (`ArrayBuffer`, `Blob`, `FormData`) becomes an empty string.

`QUERY` requests are cacheable by default (`ALLOWED_METHODS` includes `'QUERY'`), and `POST` is cacheable with `transferCache: true`. Two requests to the same URL with different binary bodies therefore share one key. On the server the second request is answered from the first one's cache entry without hitting the network, and `TransferState` ends up with a single entry holding the wrong response.

### Minimal reproduction

Server mode (`globalThis.ngServerMode = true`), `provideHttpClient()`, the transfer cache providers and `provideHttpClientTesting()`:

```ts
const body = (s: string) => Uint8Array.from(s, (c) => c.charCodeAt(0)).buffer;

http.query('/api/search', body('cats'), {responseType: 'text'}).subscribe(console.log);
httpTesting.expectOne('/api/search').flush('RESULT-FOR-CATS');

http.query('/api/search', body('dogs'), {responseType: 'text'}).subscribe(console.log);
// No second request reaches the backend; this logs 'RESULT-FOR-CATS'.
```

Expected: the second request is sent, and returns `RESULT-FOR-DOGS`.

### Proposed fix

A PR is ready: include `ArrayBuffer` and string-only `FormData` bodies in the key, and skip caching for bodies that cannot be read synchronously (`Blob`, `FormData` with files).

### Angular version

22.3.0-rc.0 and `main`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "HTTP transfer cache: QUERY/POST requests with different binary bodies share one cache key" (#72026)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): rebase Vitest incremental paths when workspace root is aliased
Issues.Body:
When `vitestConfig.root` differs from `workspaceRoot` (such as with symlinks or Windows `subst` drives), `VitestExecutor` still invalidated and queried test specifications during incremental watch-mode rebuilds using the un-rebased `workspaceRoot` paths. Because Vitest keys its module graph and test specifications against `vitest.config.root`, incremental re-runs could fail to invalidate cached modules or locate the affected test specifications.

To address this, extract a `rebasePath` helper in `plugins.ts` that converts paths between roots while leaving paths that cannot be expressed relative to the original root (such as files on a different Windows drive) unchanged instead of concatenating them. `VitestExecutor` now uses this helper during incremental rebuilds to rebase modified output and source file paths onto `vitest.config.root` when the root is aliased. Additionally, `configureVitest` now rebases from the original plugin options rather than mutating from the previous root so repeated invocations remain idempotent. `plugins_spec.ts` is expanded to cover `rebasePath`, `angular:` virtual entries, absolute setup files under coverage, and repeated `configureVitest` calls, and a new `executor_spec.ts` covers the incremental rebuild paths.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): rebase Vitest incremental paths when workspace root is aliased" (#34718)

Issues.Title: feat(@angular/build): add runnerArgs option to unit-test builder
Issues.Body:
The unit-test builder now supports a `runnerArgs` option that provides
additional command line arguments to the Vitest runner. For example,
`ng test --runner-args=--update` updates existing snapshots and
`ng test --runner-args=--bail=1` stops the run after the first failure.
The option can also be configured within the `angular.json` file.

The arguments are parsed with the Vitest command line parser and then
validated against a list of supported Vitest options. The Vitest parser
accepts unknown options, command names, and test file filters without
error. The validation ensures that a misspelled or unsupported argument
fails the build with a descriptive message instead of being ignored.
Vitest options with an equivalent builder option, such as `--reporter`
and `--coverage`, are rejected with a reference to the builder option.

The initially supported Vitest options are `--allowOnly`, `--bail`,
`--disableConsoleIntercept`, `--expandSnapshotDiff`, `--maxWorkers`,
`--printConsoleTrace`, `--retry`, `--sequence.seed`,
`--sequence.shuffle`, `--shard`, `--testTimeout`, and `--update`.

The supported options take precedence over a Vitest configuration file
but not over the other builder options. The option is not available for
the Karma runner.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(@angular/build): add runnerArgs option to unit-test builder" (#34717)

Issues.Title: test: verify snapshot updates in the Vitest snapshot e2e test
Issues.Body:
Extends the Vitest snapshot e2e test to cover updating existing snapshots after a mismatch. Vitest reads the `UPDATE_SNAPSHOT` environment variable directly, which is currently the way to request an update through `ng test` without a Vitest configuration file since the builder does not forward the `--update` flag.

The test now verifies that both the file snapshot and the inline snapshot are rewritten on disk with the new output and that a subsequent run passes without any further snapshot changes.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): resolve Vitest artifacts when workspace root is aliased
Issues.Body:
Starting in Vite 8.3.8 (`vitejs/vite@b643046`), `windowsLazyRealpathSync` calls `fs.realpathSync.native` synchronously on `config.root`, which resolves Windows `subst` drives and symlinks to their underlying physical path (e.g., `D:/.../test-project`) while the Angular CLI's `workspaceRoot` retains the logical path (`X:\test-project`).

This caused three issues during Vitest execution on aliased roots:
1. Vitest resolves relative `setupFiles` and test files against `vitestConfig.root`, which did not match `workspaceRoot` or the `testFileToEntryPoint` map in `angular:test-in-memory-provider`.
2. Passing absolute `workspaceRoot` paths in `test.include` caused `tinyglobby` (running with `cwd: vitestConfig.root`) to produce cross-drive relative paths (`../../../../X:/...`) that resolved to invalid paths (`D:/X:/...`).
3. Resolving virtual setup files under `vitestConfig.root` while resolving on-disk spec files under `workspaceRoot` caused bare package imports (such as `@angular/core/testing`) to be loaded twice from both drives.

To fix this:
- Pass workspace-relative paths in `test.include` in `VitestExecutor`.
- Rebase `workspaceRoot`, `testFileToEntryPoint`, and `setupFileSet` in `createVitestPlugins` (`configureVitest`) when `vitestConfig.root` differs from `workspaceRoot`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): resolve Vitest artifacts when workspace root is aliased" (#34714)

Issues.Title: ng build fails with 'Cannot find module @angular/core' after ng update to v22
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

21

### Description

After running `ng update @angular/cli @angular/core` to v22, `ng build` fails immediately with `Cannot find module '@angular/core'`. The project built fine on v21 before the update. Clearing node_modules and reinstalling does not fix it, and the error appears before any compilation output.

NOTE FOR LABELER: this issue is about the devkit area. Please apply the area: devkit label and set the Backlog milestone.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Create a new Angular app on v21 with `ng new repro-app`.
2. Run `ng update @angular/cli @angular/core` to v22.
3. Run `ng build`.
4. The build fails with `Cannot find module '@angular/core'`.

### Exception or Error

```text

```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.0.0Node: 22.0.0Package Manager: npmOS: Linux x64
```

### [`v0.7.2`](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/jq.bzl/releases/tag/v0.7.2)

#### Using Bzlmod with Bazel 6 or greater

1. (Bazel 6 only) Enable with `common --enable_bzlmod` in `.bazelrc`.
2. Add to your `MODULE.bazel` file:

```starlark
bazel_dep(name = "jq.bzl", version = "0.7.2")
```

#### Using WORKSPACE

Paste this snippet into your `WORKSPACE.bazel` file:

```starlark
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")
http_archive(
    name = "jq.bzl",
    sha256 = "c169a9e78d8485567753ceec9db1e76e747e1a3a4c157887a09536754b9ad547",
    strip_prefix = "jq.bzl-0.7.2",
    url = "https://github.com/bazel-contrib/jq.bzl/releases/download/v0.7.2/jq.bzl-v0.7.2.tar.gz",
)
```

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.18.0): pnpm 12.18

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.17.0...v12.18.0)

pnpm 12.18.0 packs, publishes, and installs packages with platform variants on pnpr registries. It also adds per-skill approval of agent skills and `pnpm store add` for offline installs from downloaded tarballs. Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer read the `package.json` of unchanged workspace projects. The release fixes several peer dependency resolution bugs too.

##### Minor Changes

##### Agent skills

- pnpm now names the link to a dependency's agent skill after the skill alone. A skill that the `@acme/kit` package ships in `skills/auth/` is linked as `.claude/skills/auth`, not `.claude/skills/pnpm-@acme+kit-auth`. The next install replaces links with the old names. pnpm lists the linked skills in a `# pnpm` block of each agent skill directory's `.gitignore` [#​17455](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/17455).

  When two approved packages ship a skill of the same name, or the name is already taken in an agent skill directory, pnpm links the skill as `pnpm-<package>-<skill>`. Before, the install failed.

- `pnpm approve` now asks which agent skills to link when a package ships more than one. pnpm records the chosen skills as a list, such as `permissions.<pkg>.skills: [guide, migrate]`, and does not offer the other skills for approval again. The first time a project approves a skill, `pnpm approve` also asks which agent directories to link skills into, and records the answer under `skills.dirs`.

- pnpm links agent skills nested in category directories, such as `skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md`, up to three levels below `skills/`. Before, it linked only the skills directly under `skills/`.

##### Platform variants

These features need a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`.

- `pnpm pack` packs one archive per entry of `publishConfig.variants`, each platform variant as `<name>-<version>~<tag>.tgz`. `pnpm pack --variant <target>` packs only the archive whose entry lists that target. `pnpm pack --json` prints the `integrity` and `size` of every archive it writes.

- `pnpm publish` publishes a package's `publishConfig.variants`. pnpm uploads every archive before the publish request that references them. Publishing variants to any other registry is refused unless `--no-variants` is given, which publishes only the archive that targets `any`.

- `pnpm publish --upload-variant <target>` uploads the archive of one `publishConfig.variants` entry to the registry's staging area and prints `<target>=<integrity>`. `pnpm publish --variant-integrity <target>=<integrity>` then publishes the version from archives that other jobs uploaded. With `--recursive`, each value names its package as `<name>~<target>=<integrity>`.

- `pnpm publish -r --batch` now uploads each package archive on its own request and skips archives the registry already holds, so the batch request no longer grows with the archives it publishes. A batch of more than 256 packages still carries every archive inline. Packages with `publishConfig.variants` can be published in a batch. A batch with variants that would reference more than 256 archives on one registry fails with `ERR_PNPM_BATCH_PUBLISH_TOO_MANY_ARCHIVES` [pnpm/tasks#244](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/244).

- `pnpm publish --provenance` signs one statement that names every archive of a version with `publishConfig.variants`. A platform variant's archive is named by the version's package URL with a `variant` qualifier.

- Rerunning `pnpm publish` after the version was already published now succeeds when the published version is the same release. pnpm compares the archives, the provenance statement when the rerun signs one, and the dist-tag. When the published version differs, the publish fails with `ERR_PNPM_PUBLISHED_RELEASE_DIFFERS`, which names what differs.

- pnpm installs the platform variant of a package that fits the host, or the package's own archive when none does. The lockfile records every variant. A version published with variants only, and no archive for other hosts, installs on a host one of the variants fits. On any other host, an optional dependency is skipped, and any other dependency fails with an error that lists the platforms the version is published for.

- `supportedArchitectures` platform lists accept platform tags, the same tags `publishConfig.variants` entries name. An entry can state floors and an ABI, such as `linux-x64-manylinux_2_28`, `darwin-arm64-macos_14_0`, `linux-x64-napi8` or `linux-x64-node127`, and any Node.js OS and CPU, such as `freebsd-x64`. The spellings accepted before still work.

- With `supportedArchitectures` set, pnpm also fetches into the store the variants that the other listed platforms need, when it downloads a package with platform variants.

##### pnpr registries

- pnpm downloads less metadata from a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A large package document leaves out the manifests of rarely picked versions, and pnpm fetches one only when it picks that version. In a benchmark that resolves 787 packages, the package documents shrank from 30.3 MB to 2.5 MB gzipped. pnpm caches these documents in `v12/metadata-pnpr`, and the `pnpm cache` commands cover them.

  pnpm warns when a registry that is not declared `serverType: pnpr` turns out to be pnpr. For a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`, a `minimumReleaseAge` longer than 30 days fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE`.

- `pnpm publish` sends release notes to registries declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A package's notes are the section for its version in `CHANGELOG.md`, or the notes that `pnpm version -r` composed from change intents. `--release-notes <file>` gives the notes from a file, and `--no-release-notes` sends none. `--publication-name` names a release published with `--batch`.

  In a workspace that uses pnpm's versioning, `pnpm version -r --release-notes <file>` puts a summary above the composed notes of the release.

  `pnpm view <pkg>@<version> releaseNotes`, `pnpm outdated --notes`, and `pnpm update --interactive` show the release notes from these registries.

##### Store and hooks

- `pnpm store add` now prepares the store for offline installs from package tarballs downloaded some other way. After `pnpm store add ./tarballs/*.tgz`, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` installs each registry package whose lockfile entry pins one of those tarballs [#​2978](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2978).

- Custom pnpmfile fetchers can use `fetchers.gitHostedTarball`, `fetchers.git`, and `fetchers.binary` [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Running `node` or `pnpm install` in a project that pins a Node.js version pnpm has not downloaded yet no longer hangs when a `globalPnpmfile` is configured [#​17530](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17530).

- `pnpm install` with `enableGlobalVirtualStore` no longer fails on Windows for a dependency from a named registry, such as `gh:` or `npmjs:` [#​17665](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17665).

- Concurrent installs that share a global virtual store no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_SYMLINK_BIN` when they link the same executable at the same time [#​17587](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17587).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm ci` now succeed when dependency skills are approved but no agent skill directory exists. The skills stay unlinked until a directory exists [#​17574](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17574).

- Commands run from a workspace package now use the same default store as the workspace root. Before, `pnpm add` in a package could fail with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` when the workspace root was its own mount point and the home store was on another volume, as in a sandbox or a container.

  A workspace installed with the old behavior may need one `pnpm install --force` from the workspace root.

- `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to drop such a link silently [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571).

- `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped, and `pnpm install --no-runtime` removes a runtime that an earlier install linked [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, `pnpm install` again runs a dependency's build scripts in a project whose global virtual store slot another project already built, unless the side-effects cache has build output to restore for it. A build that writes only outside its own package, such as a git hook installer, now takes effect in every project [#​17526](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17526).

- Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586).

- Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal.

##### Lockfile and local paths

- Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts a lockfile written with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when `addMissingPeerTypes` is enabled and an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#​17668](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17668).

- Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691).

  Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory.

- Relative local paths in root catalogs now resolve for dependencies and peers [#​17690](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17690).

- `pnpm install` now resolves auto-installed relative `workspace:` and `file:` peers from the directory of the package that declares them [#​17676](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17676), [#​17689](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17689).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` leaves `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched while it looks for deduplication changes. If `configDependencies` changed since the last install, the check keeps the lockfile they sync, as `pnpm install` does [#​17628](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17628).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is the integrity of a locked version that the registry now reports with a stronger algorithm, such as a `sha512` integrity replacing the `sha1` shasum it reported when the lockfile was written [#​17692](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17692).

##### Peer dependencies

- Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666).

- Dependencies no longer bind to another project's peer variant when the provider has nested peers, including providers that finish resolving later [#​17593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17593).

- Re-resolving a lockfile no longer preserves optional peer bindings from other projects when no provider is in scope [#​17592](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17592).

- `pnpm peers check` warns when a required peer is resolved without a provider declared by the project or its dependency ancestors, with `autoInstallPeers: false` and `dedupePeerDependents: true`. These warnings do not change the command's exit code or cause `strictPeerDependencies` failures.

##### Speed and memory

- `pnpm install`, and `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, no longer read the `package.json` of workspace projects whose files did not change since the last install. This also holds with a pnpmfile, `configDependencies`, or `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. In an up-to-date workspace with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` no longer runs the install of each project [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- A recursive `pnpm run` or `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun` set no longer reads every `package.json` in the workspace once per project when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. In a 300-project workspace, `pnpm -r exec true` went from 490 ms to 42 ms [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- `pnpm install` makes fewer `stat` calls when it hardlinks files from the store, as few as 12.7.0 made [#​17543](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17543).

- Picking versions from registry metadata uses less temporary memory.

##### verifyDepsBeforeRun and repeat installs

- With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports a `file:` directory dependency as out of date after an edit to `package.json` that leaves its dependencies unchanged [#​17697](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17697).

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first.

- A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm add <pkg>` without a version now saves the range that the other workspace projects declare for the package, or the one a matching override sets. A `catalog:` reference still comes first, and the `tag` setting is used only when none of these exists [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

- `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged. Negated `crate:` and `pypi:` selectors, such as `!crate:sha2`, now exclude that dependency and update the rest [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243).

- `pnpm update --latest` keeps three kinds of Cargo dependencies where they are, unless the crate is named on the command line. Before, it moved each one to the newest release and left a workspace that did not build.

  - A renamed dependency, such as `tower-0-4 = { package = "tower", version = "0.4" }`, stays within its requirement if the workspace also declares the crate under its own name.
  - A crate replaced through `[patch.crates-io]` keeps its version, with a warning.
  - A crate whose newest release is older than its current version, such as a prerelease newer than the latest stable release, keeps its version, with a warning. Only an explicit version, such as `pnpm update crate:foo@1`, moves it back.

  Other new major versions are still selected and may need code changes.

- `pnpm update` now keeps a Cargo dependency at its current version, with a warning, if the new version lacks a feature the workspace enables on it. If the crate is named on the command line, as in `pnpm update --latest crate:sha2`, the update fails with an error that names the missing features.

- `pnpm update` now keeps the operator of every existing Cargo requirement, so `~1.0.0` is updated to `~1.1.0`, and an exact `=` requirement stays exact unless the selector gives a range, such as `crate:foo@^2`. The `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings apply only to new Cargo dependencies. Saved Cargo requirements omit build metadata.

- `pnpm update` now updates a Cargo dependency whose inline table spans several lines, such as one with a multi-line `features` array. It failed with "its Cargo.toml dependency declaration is not a string or single-line inline table".

- `pnpm update` no longer applies the `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings to Python requirements. A `savePrefix` such as `^` made `pnpm update` fail in a project with Python dependencies.

  `pnpm update` now keeps the precision of a `~=` requirement, so `~=1.0` is updated to `~=1.5` and still allows any 1.x release. With `--latest`, a `==1.*` requirement is updated to `==2.*`.

##### Store

- `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230).

- `pnpm store prune` now removes aliases of pruned packages.

- `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631).

- `pnpm store add` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to write package files into the read-only store without recording them, so no install could use them.

- `pnpm cat-index <name>@<version>` no longer shows the index of a package whose name differs only in letter case.

##### Other commands and settings

- `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- `pnpm link <dir>` now resolves a relative `<dir>` against the current directory. In a directory without a `package.json`, such as a workspace's `packages` folder, `pnpm link .` used to link the nearest project above it into itself [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516).

- Switching to the pnpm version a project pins no longer writes a temporary `_tmp_*` file into the project directory, which file watchers reported on every command [#​17681](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17681).

- pnpm now reads the `linkWorkspacePackages`, `injectWorkspacePackages`, `extendNodePath`, `frozenStore`, and `optimisticRepeatInstall` settings from `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_LINK_WORKSPACE_PACKAGES=true`. `--config.extend-node-path` now applies too.

- Recursive scripts run with `--sequential` or `--workspace-concurrency=1` print GitHub Actions log groups again [#​17629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17629).

- When `pnpm docs` cannot open a browser, the URL it prints no longer includes the query string or the fragment.

### [`v12.17.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.17.0): pnpm 12.17

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.1...v12.17.0)

pnpm 12.17.0 adds `pnpm peers check --global`, dependency-group selectors and wildcards in `overrides`, and runtime, package manager, Cargo, and Python updates in `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update`. It also fixes files that other users could not read in Docker images, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm peers check` now accepts `--global` (`-g`) to check globally installed packages. After a global install or update, the peer dependency warning now suggests `pnpm peers check -g` [#​17504](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17504).

- `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` now inspect and update package manager and runtime versions in `devEngines.packageManager`, `packageManager`, `devEngines.runtime`, `engines.runtime`, and `runtime:` dependencies. With `cargo.enabled` or `python.enabled`, `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` also inspect and update Cargo dependencies in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` and Python dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and `pylock.toml`.

- `overrides` selectors now support `:prod`, `:optional`, and `:peer` pseudo-selectors that target a single dependency group. They also support `*` wildcard patterns on parent and target package names. An override with a non-range value, such as `npm:` or `file:`, no longer adds a peer dependency to `dependencies`. Removing an optional dependency with `"-"` now also removes the duplicate entry from `dependencies` [#​5391](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5391).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Files that pnpm creates in a project now get the permissions the umask gives any new file, such as `0644`. Before, several of them were readable only by the user who ran pnpm, which broke Docker images that run as a different user [#​17435](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17435).

  The fix applies to:

  - `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. A different user running `pnpm run` reinstalled the dependencies because it could not read this file.
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
  - the files written by `pnpm deploy`
  - patch files from `pnpm patch-commit`
  - the lockfile restored by `pnpm dedupe --check`
  - the Cargo and Python files that pnpm writes

  When pnpm edits an existing file, the file keeps its permissions.

- `pnpm install` no longer writes broken dependency links when the project's `node_modules` is a symlink to another directory, such as another project's `node_modules`. The install reported success, but the links it wrote did not resolve [#​17448](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17448).

- Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#​17503](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503).

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, it now installs that version's native binary for the current host, even if the project's `supportedArchitectures` excludes the host. Before, pnpm could not use the pinned version and kept running the installed one. pnpm also repairs a pinned version that an earlier install left without the host's binary.

- With the global virtual store, a change to a dependency of one package in a dependency cycle now gives every package in that cycle a new directory. Before, the other packages kept their directories and still linked the old copy of the changed package, so the project could load two copies of it [#​17466](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17466).

  Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once.

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, when two workspace projects need the same package version and it cannot be hoisted to the root, each project now keeps the copy installed in its own `node_modules`. Build scripts run in each of these copies. Before, the second project's copy was replaced with a symlink to the first project's, so every repeat install imported it again [#​17498](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17498).

- The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#​17490](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490).

- Hardlinking from the store now stats each store file once per install. Since pnpm 12.8.0, a store file was stat'ed again for every package that links it. On an offline install of a large workspace, that added up to 15% system CPU [#​17500](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17500).

##### Repeat installs and local dependencies

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer reports an outdated lockfile right after the install that wrote it. This happened when a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook or `packageExtensions` changed the dependencies or peer dependencies of a local directory dependency outside the workspace projects. It affected a `file:` dependency, an injected `workspace:../dir` dependency outside the workspace patterns, and an injected workspace package left out by `--filter` [#​17447](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17447) [#​17473](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17473).

  A repeat `pnpm install` now takes the fast path when `ignoredOptionalDependencies` removes an optional dependency of a `file:` directory dependency. It used to resolve again on every run.

- `pnpm install` now resolves again after an edit to an injected `workspace:../dir` dependency outside the workspace patterns under a shared lockfile. It used to keep the lockfile unchanged. The next `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then failed [#​17476](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17476).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#​17486](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486).

- With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before.

- `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A repeat install reported "Already up to date" and kept the old contents before [pnpm/tasks#227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/227).

- `pnpm install` now relinks a `workspace:` or `link:` dependency whose link was deleted from `node_modules`. It used to report "Already up to date" and leave the link missing [#​17485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17485).

- A repeat `pnpm install` reports "Already up to date" again when a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook changes the dependencies of a workspace project. Since 12.15.0, every such install ran in full [#​17468](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17468).

  After an edit to a project's `package.json`, `pnpm install` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now run the pnpmfile's `readPackage` hook on the edited manifest before comparing it with the lockfile. They could report the project up to date when the hook rewrote the edited dependency to a specifier the lockfile did not record.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm update --latest` with package selectors now updates the dependencies of the selected packages within their declared ranges. Excluded packages and their dependencies keep their locked versions [#​17444](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17444).

- `pnpm add <pkg>@<tag>` now uses a catalog entry set to that same dist-tag. The dependency is saved as `catalog:` and the entry stays as written [pnpm/tasks#225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/225).

  When `pnpm add` adds a new dist-tag such as `vue@legacy` to a catalog, the catalog entry records the exact version the tag points to. The same applies to a dependency added without a version when the `tag` setting names a dist-tag other than `latest`.

- `pnpm add` now saves the resolved version range of an npm alias. For example, `pnpm add v2@npm:vue` and `pnpm add v2@npm:vue@^3.0.0` both save `npm:vue@^3.5.13`.

##### Running scripts and commands

- Programs that a script or `pnpm exec` command leaves running, such as a browser opened by the `open` package, now outlive pnpm exactly when they would outlive the command run without pnpm. Before, on Windows, a failed command, `Ctrl+C`, or a closed terminal ended all of them. pnpm still ends them when it is killed or crashes.

  When a recursive or parallel run bails, the scripts still running now receive `SIGTERM` on Unix and are killed only if they are still running two seconds later. On Windows, everything those scripts started is ended, including detached processes whose parent has already exited. Before, a bail killed them at once [#​17465](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17465).

- On Windows, the shell shim of a `.cmd` or `.bat` bin now runs it under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion is off, such as with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`. The shim used to start an interactive cmd.exe prompt [#​17480](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17480).

- `pnx` and `pnpm create` now run the command in the directory selected by `--dir` or `--workspace-root`. Without either flag, the command still runs in the directory pnpm was started in.

- `pnpm --env-file` now reads files the way `node --env-file` does. Values are taken as written, so `$VAR` is no longer expanded and Windows paths such as `C:\Users\me` load unchanged. A file is no longer rejected for its contents.

##### Settings and messages

- `pnpm version` no longer creates a git commit and tag when `gitTagVersion` is set to `false` [#​17460](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17460).

- `pnpm publish` now reads the `publishBranch` setting from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and from `PNPM_CONFIG_PUBLISH_BRANCH`. The `--publish-branch` flag overrides it.

- `pnpm` now accepts `--strict-ssl` and `--local-address <ip>` on the command line.

- `pnpm doctor` uses a 15-second timeout when checking registry connectivity.

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` parse errors now report `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING`.

- The error for a dependency with an invalid name in a project's manifest now names the project's directory. It used to say only "The current package", which did not tell which workspace project to fix [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

The `ng-packagr` builder (`@angular/build:ng-packagr`) and its programmatic APIs (`executeNgPackagrBuilder` and `NgPackagrBuilderOptions`) are not marked as deprecated, and `@angular-devkit/build-angular:ng-packagr` recommends `@angular/build:ng-packagr`.

- Logs a runtime deprecation warning when executing `@angular/build:ng-packagr` recommending `@angular/build:library`.
- Updates `@angular-devkit/build-angular:ng-packagr` deprecation warning to point directly to `@angular/build:library`.
- Marks `executeNgPackagrBuilder`, `NgPackagrBuilderOptions`, and `ng-packagr`-related workspace model symbols as `@deprecated` across `@angular/build`, `@angular-devkit/build-angular`, and `@schematics/angular`, and updates public API goldens.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add a TODO for negated arrayWithExactContents in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
`transformArrayWithExactContents` splits the assertion into a `.toHaveLength()` check and a `.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining())` check without looking for `.not`. A negated assertion is split into two negated checks, which asserts that neither condition holds instead of not both: an array with the right length but different contents passes in Jasmine and fails after the migration.

Vitest has no single matcher for exact-contents-in-any-order, so a faithful negation cannot be expressed by splitting. Leave the negated form unchanged and add a TODO comment instead, matching the existing handling of a dynamic (non-literal) argument.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@schematics/angular): add a TODO for negated arrayWithExactContents in refactor-jasmine-vitest" (#34691)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): handle pending() in focused and skipped tests in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
`transformPending` only matches calls whose expression is the bare `it` identifier, but `transformFocusedAndSkippedTests` runs earlier in the pipeline and has already renamed `fit` to `it.only` and `xit` to `it.skip`. A focused test containing `pending()` is therefore migrated to `it.only` with the `pending()` call left in place, which throws a ReferenceError at runtime since Vitest has no `pending` global; a skipped test keeps a dangling `pending()` call that no longer compiles once the Jasmine types are removed.

Also match the renamed `it.only` and `it.skip` forms and convert both to `it.skip` with the usual TODO comment. A pending spec never runs its body in Jasmine, even when focused, so `it.skip` preserves the observed behavior.

Verified with two new `transformPending` cases that run the full transform pipeline on `fit` and `xit` inputs; both fail without this change and `//packages/schematics/angular:test` passes with it.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@schematics/angular): handle pending() in focused and skipped tests in refactor-jasmine-vitest" (#34689)

Issues.Title: fix(material/core): use neutral-variant 80 for dark on-surface-variant
Issues.Body:
Maps `on-surface-variant` in the dark scheme back to `neutral-variant` tone 80, matching material-color-utilities, the material-web tokens and the output of the `theme-color` schematic.

#29655 changed this value to tone 90 based on a Theme Builder label that did not match the rendered color (material-foundation/material-theme-builder#301). #29902 already reverted another change from that PR, which was based on a mislabeled swatch as well.

Fixes #34134

Issues.Title: bug(material/core): dark on-surface-variant uses neutral-variant 90 instead of 80
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

18.1.x

### Description

In the dark scheme, `on-surface-variant` maps to `neutral-variant` tone 90 ([`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24)). The Material color spec maps it to tone 80:

- [material-color-utilities `color_spec_2021.ts`](https://github.com/material-foundation/material-color-utilities/blob/main/typescript/dynamiccolor/color_spec_2021.ts): `onSurfaceVariant` → `tone: (s) => s.isDark ? 80 : 30`, unchanged since 2023.
- [material-web tokens v0_192](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/v0_192/_md-sys-color.scss): `neutral-variant80`.
- The `theme-color` schematic in this repo bundles material-color-utilities and therefore generates tone 80, so its output disagrees with the system tokens in the same package.

Tone 90 came in with #29655, which followed #29577. That issue relied on Theme Builder screenshots, and the Theme Builder labeled the dark `On Surface Var.` swatch "NV-90". That label was wrong: the swatch itself is tone 80, as already reported in material-foundation/material-theme-builder#301 (May 2024). The pixels in the screenshot attached to #29577 confirm this. The same PR changed `surface-container-highest` because of a mislabeled swatch, and #29902 reverted that change.

Because the tones are equal, `on-surface` and `on-surface-variant` render identically in the dark scheme whenever the neutral and neutral-variant palettes are close or equal. As a result, form field placeholders look like entered values, and labels and hint texts lose their visual hierarchy.

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz reproduction: the wrong value is a static token mapping and can be read directly in [`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24).

To see the effect:

1. Generate a theme with `ng generate @angular/material:theme-color` and the same color for neutral and neutral-variant, e.g. `#ececed`.
2. Render a `mat-form-field` with `appearance="outline"`, a placeholder and `floatLabel="always"`, next to a filled one, in the dark scheme.

### Expected Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to `neutral-variant` tone 80 in the dark scheme. Placeholders are visibly dimmer than entered values.

### Actual Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to tone 90, the same tone as `--mat-sys-on-surface`. Placeholders and values are indistinguishable.

### Environment

- Angular Material: 22.2.6
- Still present on `main` (fcec64761)

Issues.Title: Autocomplete can select an option after being disabled while open
Issues.Body:
### Reproduction

1. Attach an Angular Material autocomplete with Apple and Orange options to a reactive form input. Start with Apple selected.
2. Use a timer to call `control.disable()` in two seconds. Focus the input before the timer fires so the panel opens.
3. After the input is disabled, click Orange in the panel.

The input changes to Orange and `optionSelected` fires. The same happens if the timer sets `matAutocompleteDisabled` to true instead.

Disabling either the form control or autocomplete should close the existing suggestions without selecting an option. With `matAutocompleteDisabled`, the user should still be able to type in the plain input.

Reproduced on Angular Components main at `32cf96285` in Chrome on macOS. Issues.Title: fix(cdk/scrolling): prevent nested tables from inheriting outer viewport
Issues.Body:
Hi! This fixes ordinary tables inside `*cdkVirtualFor` items throwing `CdkVirtualScrollViewport is already attached.` on initial render.

Fixes #34121.

### What changes

An inner table can resolve the outer `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` token and enable table virtualization, even though `cdkVirtualFor` already owns that viewport.

Provide `null` for this token on `CdkVirtualForOf`, alongside the existing `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` boundary introduced in #34100. This lets tables inside the repeated items render normally. The repeater itself resolves its owning viewport using `skipSelf`, and an independent nested viewport provides its own token.

This also means custom consumers of `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` inside virtual-for items resolve `null` instead of implicitly inheriting the outer viewport.

### Regression coverage

Add a test with ordinary tables inside virtual-for items. It checks that each table renders all of its rows without virtual-table fixed layout, both initially and after scrolling. It also checks that the outer viewport retains the correct data length and advances its rendered range.

Before the fix, the new test fails with the reported error; the other 89 CDK table tests pass.

### Validation

Completed locally:

- CDK table: Chromium (90 passed) and Firefox (90 passed).
- CDK scrolling: Chromium (109 passed).
- Material table: Chromium (36 passed).
- Repository formatter, targeted TSLint, and `git diff --check`.

The standalone reproduction linked in #34121 was also verified in Chrome using published Angular/CDK 22.2.6.
